blocks.content: 1. WHAT IS A VERB?

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Verbs are categorized into Finite vs Non-Finite verbs as well as Main and Helping (Auxiliary) verbs.
Auxiliary helping verbs include 'BE', 'HAVE', and 'DO', with 'DO' being a primary area for error detection.
Modal verbs cover key distinctions such as CAN vs COULD, MAY vs MIGHT, MUST, SHALL vs WILL, WOULD, SHOULD, OUGHT TO, and USED TO.
Need and Dare form an advanced yet critical section of auxiliary verbs for competitive exams.
Targeted practice of SSC Golden Rules is essential for solving exam-level error detection questions.

blocks.content:
A verb is a word that expresses an action, state, feeling, or occurrence. It tells us what the subject of the sentence does or what happens to it.



A sentence without a verb is incomplete because the verb acts as the engine of the sentence.



Examples:

• The child plays.

• She is happy.

• They were dancing.

• The glass broke.



⭐ EXAM INSIGHT:

Nearly 60–70% of grammar questions in SSC are directly or indirectly connected with verbs because tense, voice, narration, and subject‑verb agreement all depend on verbs.



👉 Golden Rule: No finite verb = No complete sentence.
2. FINITE vs NON-FINITE VERBS

Before moving ahead, it is important to understand the difference between finite and non‑finite verbs.



FINITE VERBS:

A finite verb changes according to tense and subject.

Example:

• She writes a letter.

• She wrote a letter.



NON‑FINITE VERBS:

They do not change with tense or subject.



Types:

• Infinitive – to write

• Gerund – writing

• Participle – written / writing



⭐ SSC TIP:

Error detection questions often test whether the verb properly agrees with the subject and tense — which only finite verbs do.
3. TYPES OF VERBS (SSC CLASSIFICATION)

For competitive exams, verbs are primarily divided into three major categories:



1. Main Verb

2. Helping Verb (Auxiliary Verb)

3. Modal Verb



Understanding this classification is extremely important because many spotting error questions are based on incorrect auxiliary usage.
4. MAIN VERB

A main verb expresses the primary action or state of the subject.



Examples:

• He runs fast.

• She enjoys music.

• The baby slept peacefully.



Here, runs, enjoys, and slept are main verbs because they carry the central meaning of the sentence.
4.1 FORMS OF VERB (VERY VERY IMPORTANT FOR SSC)

Every English verb has five important forms:



V1 – Base Form → go

V2 – Past Form → went

V3 – Past Participle → gone

V‑ing – Present Participle → going

s/es – Singular Present → goes



⭐ WHERE SSC USES THESE:

• Tense questions

• Active–Passive Voice

• Narration

• Fill in the blanks

• Error Detection



👉 Golden Rule:

After DID → always use V1.

Incorrect: He did not went.

Correct: He did not go.
5. HELPING VERBS (AUXILIARY VERBS)

Helping verbs support the main verb to form tense, voice, mood, or emphasis.



PRIMARY AUXILIARIES:

• Be → is, am, are, was, were, been, being

• Have → has, have, had

• Do → do, does, did



Without auxiliaries, advanced sentence structures would not be possible.
5.1 USE OF ‘BE’

AS A MAIN VERB:

• She is a doctor.

• They were tired.



AS A HELPING VERB:

• She is studying.

• They were playing.



⭐ SSC TRAP:

Students often forget that “being” and “been” are also forms of BE used in passive voice and perfect continuous tense.
5.2 USE OF ‘HAVE’

1. Possession:

• I have a car.



2. Perfect Tense:

• She has completed her assignment.

• They had left before we arrived.



3. Compulsion (Have to):

• I have to submit the form today.



⭐ IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE:

Have → possession

Have to → obligation.
5.3 USE OF ‘DO’ (SSC ERROR KING)

1. To form negatives:

• I do not agree.



2. To ask questions:

• Do you understand?



3. For emphasis:

• I do want to help you.



👉 GOLDEN RULE:

Did + V1



Wrong: She did not completed the work.

Correct: She did not complete the work.
6. MODAL VERBS

Modals are special helping verbs that express ability, permission, probability, advice, obligation, or necessity.



COMMON MODALS:

Can, Could, May, Might, Shall, Should, Will, Would, Must, Ought to



👉 SUPER GOLDEN RULE:

Modal + V1 (always)



Wrong: She can sings.

Correct: She can sing.
6.1 CAN vs COULD

rows: Degree of probability and formal permission

blocks.content:
CAN:

• Ability → I can swim.

• Informal permission → Can I sit here?



COULD:

• Past ability → I could run fast when I was young.

• Polite request → Could you please help me?



⭐ SSC TRAP:

I cannot be able to solve this. ❌

I cannot solve this. ✅

I will not be able to solve this. ✅
6.2 MAY vs MIGHT

MAY → Strong possibility

• It may rain tonight.



MIGHT → Weak possibility

• He might miss the train.



⭐ EXAM NOTE:

“Might” is often preferred when the sentence is in past context.
6.3 MUST

Uses of MUST:



1. Compulsion:

Candidates must carry ID proof.



2. Strong deduction:

The lights are off — they must be sleeping.



3. Duty:

A soldier must obey orders.
7. SHALL vs WILL

Traditional Grammar:

I / We → Shall

Others → Will



Modern Usage:

Will is commonly used with all subjects.



SPECIAL USES:

• Determination → I will succeed.

• Command → You shall follow the rules.

• Promise → I will support you.
8. WOULD

1. Past Habit:

When we were children, we would play outside for hours.



2. Polite Request:

Would you open the window?



3. Imaginary Condition:

If I were rich, I would travel the world.
9. SHOULD, OUGHT TO & USED TO

items: Forms of verb are crucial for SSC exam pattern questions.
The use of 'DO' requires careful study as it is heavily tested in error spotting.
Differentiate modal usage clearly: CAN vs COULD, MAY vs MIGHT, and SHALL vs WILL.

blocks.content:
SHOULD → Advice

You should revise daily.



OUGHT TO → Moral duty

We ought to help the needy.



USED TO → Past habit

She used to live here.



⭐ SSC TRAP:

He uses to smoke ❌

He used to smoke ✅
10. NEED & DARE (ADVANCED BUT IMPORTANT)

Need and Dare can act both as main verbs and modal verbs.



As Modal:

• You need not worry.

• He dare not oppose me.



As Main Verb:

• You need to work hard.

• He dared to speak the truth.
11. MOST IMPORTANT SSC GOLDEN RULES

✔ Modal + V1

✔ Did + V1

✔ Never use “be able to” with can

✔ Used to = past only

✔ Must have + V3 = past assumption



Example:

He must have forgotten the meeting.
12. PRACTICE QUESTIONS (SSC LEVEL)

Error Detection:

1. He did not knew the answer.

2. She can sings very well.

3. He uses to play football.



Fill in the blanks:

1. You ___ obey the rules. (must / can)

2. ___ you help me with this file? (would / shall)

3. She did not ___ the letter. (write / wrote)



Answers: know, sing, used to, must, would, write.
